title: URL Shortener with click analytics
summary: HTTP API that creates short links for long URLs (optionally with a custom alias), redirects visitors to the original URL and reports per-link click analytics.

functionalRequirements.description: Create a short link for an absolute http/https URL; the service generates a unique short code.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: POST /api/v1/urls with a valid URL returns 201 with the code, the short URL and a Location header; invalid URLs (non-http(s), malformed, embedded credentials, longer than 2048 chars) return 400 problem details.

functionalRequirements.description: Optionally choose a custom alias instead of a generated code.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: Aliases of 4-32 characters [A-Za-z0-9_-] are accepted; an alias already in use returns 409; reserved words (api, health, ops) are rejected with 400.

functionalRequirements.description: Visiting a short link redirects to the original URL.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: GET /{code} returns 302 with Location set to the target URL; an unknown code returns 404.

functionalRequirements.description: Record every redirect as a click (timestamp, referrer host, user-agent family) without slowing the redirect.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: Clicks are recorded asynchronously and appear in the statistics within a few seconds; no raw IP address is stored.

functionalRequirements.description: Report click analytics per link: total clicks, clicks per day and top referrers.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: GET /api/v1/urls/{code}/stats returns totalClicks, daily counts for the requested window (default 30 days) and the top 10 referrers; unknown code returns 404.

functionalRequirements.description: Look up a short link's metadata.
functionalRequirements.acceptance: GET /api/v1/urls/{code} returns code, short URL, target URL, creation time and click count; unknown code returns 404.

nfr.notes: Must stay fast and reliable under load: redirects are the hot, read-heavy path; analytics must not add latency to redirects.

assumptions: Anonymous API: link creation needs no authentication in this version (abuse is limited by per-client rate limiting).
Redirects use 302 (not 301) so browsers do not cache them and every click is counted.
Links do not expire in this version.
Analytics store referrer host and user-agent family only (data minimisation).
